subject: Discovery Recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Tan <alex.tan@finbot.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro & quick demo

Thanks again for the demo today, Marissa - helpful overview. A quick recap from our side and a few clarifying items.

Key pain points we mentioned:
- Token/unit cost on peak inference: current monthly spend is spiking with our realtime scoring (up to ~1.2M tokens/day).
- Tail latency for interactive flows (esp. low-traffic regions).
- Operational burden around versioned rollouts and QA for output quality.

Current stack:
- Model: on-prem BERT-2.1-based encoder for embeddings; experimenting with open autoregressive models for assistants.
- Serving: Kubernetes + in-house autoscaling, limited GPU pooling.
- Caching: custom Redis prefix cache for short-term session context, no KV cache for transformer decoders yet.

Success criteria we care about:
1) 2x reduction in per-token cost or same cost with 2x throughput.
2) P95 latency < 250ms for single-turn assistant calls.
3) Smooth model rollouts with canary and fallback to smaller quantized models.

Questions / next steps:
- Can you share typical unit economics assumptions (tokens/hour, batching gains) and any reference cost model?
- What quantization options do you support out-of-the-box? How invasive is model conversion?
- Would love a quick ping on Dedicated vs Hosted pricing for ~500k tokens/day baseline.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of ML Engineering, FinBot
[Attachment: cost_model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Alex Tan <alex.tan@finbot.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Samantha - thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the cost spreadsheet. Couple notes from our side and proposals for next steps.

Quick answers to your questions:
- Unit economics: I attached a short reference model (redwood_inference_one_pager.pdf) but high level: batching + prefix KV cache typically drives 1.5-3x effective improvement in tokens/sec depending on request shape. For streaming assistant workloads with short contexts we often see 25-40% reduction in cost once KV caching is leveraged.
- Quantization: we support int8 and more aggressive 4-bit (Q4) variants for many open models; conversion is usually a 1-2 step pipeline we can run for you. For proprietary / highly-customized weights we run verification tests on-held infrastructure before rollout.
- Dedicated vs Hosted: for your baseline (500k tokens/day) Hosted is faster to start; Dedicated reserved pools become cost-effective as you commit to sustained throughput (we can run numbers in the model you shared).

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood: run a quick cost-sensitivity model using your sheet (I will update the attached file with our numbers).
2) Technical spike: small PoC to test batching + KV caching on a subset of your traffic (2-4 weeks). Ben from our infra team will own this.
3) Quantization readiness: we can run a compatibility pass on one model (non-prod) to estimate accuracy delta - low-effort sample.

Could you confirm: who on your side owns procurement / contract questions? We will include procurement in the next thread so we can scope SOW and pricing.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_inference_one_pager.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha@finbot.ai>, procurement@finbot.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps

Appreciate the summary, Marissa. Procurement is procurement@finbot.ai (CC'd). We're good to move forward with the PoC scope - primary objectives are: validate cost reductions for peak inference, measure P95 latency improvements, and observe any quality delta from int8/Q4.

Two logistical notes:
- Timeline: target PoC start 04/20, duration 3 weeks.
- Access: we'll provision a small test cluster and a service account (details to follow).

I uploaded the spreadsheet with expected traffic distributions - please import your assumptions and share the updated model.

Best,
Alex
Product Ops, FinBot
